newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hanwa won't cause financial system worries - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Hanwa won't cause financial system worries - MOF.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Thursday he did not think the case of ailing Hanwa Bank Ltd would bring about any anxiety concerning the overall financial system in Japan.
"I don't think the case of Hanwa will bring about anxiety about Japan's overall financial system," Mitsuzuka told a news conference.
He said all depositors would be fully protected.

An inspection by the ministry earlier had shown that Hanwa Bank had net liabilities, and the ministry had been planning to disclose the suspension after Hanwa released its earnings report for the half-year to September on Friday.
Mitsuzuka said newspaper reports about the ministry's plan to order a suspension of Hanwa's business had prompted the minstry to issue such an order today to prevent confusion among depositors.
Japan's Deposit Insurance Corp would provide funds to help cover withdrawals of deposits, a ministry official said.

Funds available from the Deposit Insurance Corp over the next five years to cover Hanwa and any future failures of financial institutions would total 2.7 trillion yen, the ministry official told reporters.

A bank which would be set up to wind up Hanwa and take over its assets would not be a permanent body, but there was a possibility that the bank would be used as a vehicle to cope with future bank failures, the official said.
The bank would be financed mainly by a special fund recently created within the deposit insurance system aimed at stabilising Japan's financial system, the official said.

The ministry had been unable to find any private banks that could take over the business of Hanwa Bank, but there would be cases in the future where healthy institutions took over assets of failed banks, he said.
The details of the wind-up bank for Hanwa would be discussed later by the parties involved, including the Deposit Insurance Corp, the official said.
The ministry would inform other major nations through their embassies in Tokyo of Thursday's announcement involving Hanwa.
